## Test-evidence correction (supersedes the "Gates" paragraph of my earlier comment)

My earlier comment named ONE unrelated pre-existing failure. That was incomplete, and the
"targeted suites pass / zero failures locally" phrasing was weaker evidence than it sounded.
Correcting the record.

**What went wrong with my local runs.** I twice started the full unit suite and then moved the
repo HEAD underneath it (`git commit`, then `git reset --hard` after the server-side rebase,
then removed the worktree). Both runs are therefore invalid: the first reported HEAD-move
errors naming exactly my own commit and reset, and the second reached 100% but died at teardown
with `FileNotFoundError` on the deleted directory. I had been grepping for `FAILED:` summary
lines that those crashed runs never got far enough to write, which is why they looked clean.

**Proper verification.** I re-ran on an undisturbed checkout of the merged commit
(859b… "a573: remove the inert code-health off switch") in an isolated worktree. Exactly THREE
tests fail there, identified by mapping progress-stream positions to the deterministic
`-p no:randomly` collection order:

- `tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present`
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone`
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_loc_heldout.py::test_live`

**Discriminating experiment.** I built a second worktree at the PARENT commit (9100 "mark
generated surfaces as generated") — a tree that still HAS `CodeHealthConfig.enabled`, asserted
at runtime — provisioned an identical venv, and ran the same three tests. They fail
**identically**, same assertions and same errors (`assert 'metric' in {...}`, `assert 0 >= 1`,
`KeyError: 'sample.py'`). So all three are pre-existing and independent of this change.

They are also environment-specific: the local venv is Python **3.14.6**, which CI does not
test (the matrix is 3.11/3.12/3.13 plus macOS 3.13), and the two `_heldout` "live" tests shell
out to the external `scc` / `jscpd` binaries, whose local versions drift from what the fixtures
expect.

**The authoritative signal is unchanged and green:** CI ran the full suite on four clean
checkouts and passed, yielding `Verified +1` alongside `LLM-Review +1` (clean PASS), and the
change merged. Nothing here changes the outcome — it just replaces a soft claim with a
properly attributed one.
